observation.visible_scene: An indoor corner with a tall pyramid built from colorful plastic grid-blocks (yellow top, then blue/orange, orange/white/blue, white/blue/yellow/blue, and a bottom row of blue/yellow/blue/orange/white cubes) standing against a white wall. To the right is a window whose sill holds a long row of small upright colored pieces; the glass shows a dim reflection of the room (a yellow cap-like shape and a metallic bowl). On the left is a white folding table with flat block layouts, a glowing neon sign reading partially 'IGN / LD / PLE!', a box, and a heap of loose white/colored pieces on the floor. The foreground floor has a arranged mosaic of red, orange and maroon block squares bordered in black. The scene is essentially a still setup.
visible_changes: The block pyramid, the floor mosaic, the table contents, the loose-piece pile and the neon sign stay physically unchanged throughout the excerpt: no block moves, shifts, falls or is added.

A slow, slight camera drift is present: comparing frame 1 to frame 41, all scene content moves gradually rightward in the image (e.g., the window's left edge shifts from roughly x=545 to x=640, and the top yellow block from x=470 to x=482), consistent with a gentle pan/zoom rather than any object motion.
The row of colored pieces on the window sill and the reflection inside the glass translate together with the rest of the frame (camera motion), not independently.
No collapse, trigger, contact or completion occurs within this segment; the structure remains intact from first to last sampled frame.
outside_clip_unknowns: Whether the pyramid later topples or is triggered (this appears to be a Hevesh-style setup, but the cause/onset and any outcome lie outside the cropped segment).
What the reflected figure/person in the window is doing, since it is only a reflection and not directly observed.
Any motion before t=0 or after the last frame.
uncertain_details: The exact nature of the camera movement (pan vs. slight zoom-out vs. dolly) is hard to disambiguate from the subtle background shift.
Whether any tiny vibration of the blocks is present is not resolvable at this sampling rate; visually the structure is static.
